summary: Tested mark_non_script fix, the dry-run key validate endpoint, tts/status eleven_blocked_voices, the Settings 'Testar' button and data-current in ScriptView. Passing: e1_tests/test_tscheck_settings_nonbelong.py (all, including test_similar_dialogue_not_marked_header), round7 TestPaged (7 auto-marked), the validate endpoint (invalid -> valid:false, saved:false, keys unchanged, 404, 400), tts/status list, the uppercase stage direction that is repeated irregularly (not marked), the Settings UI and data-current. FAILING: (1) the ROOT BUG IS STILL OPEN when the repeats are regularly spaced. PEDRO: 'Sim.' x3 (every 3 lines) and MARIA: 'Não.' x4 (every 4 lines) are still turned into foreign lines and lose their speaker. (2) A repeated footer 'Texto de João Silva' next to page numbers is NOT marked.

critical.issue: Dialogue that repeats at regular intervals is still auto-marked foreign and loses its speaker. For dialogue, the grouping key text is built as f'{character} — {text}'. That string always contains '—', so RE_HEADER_WORD matches and _header_like() is always True for dialogue. The positional check then passes through _regular(pos) (gaps >=3 and max<=2*min), which is common in a real back-and-forth. Repro: 3 rounds of [ANA q, PEDRO: Sim., RUI c] -> idx 1,4,7 become foreign 'PEDRO — Sim.'. Same for 4 rounds of MARIA: Não. at gap 4.

minor.issue: The regex r'^(de|por|texto de|by)\s+...' is case-sensitive, so 'Texto de João Silva' / 'De João Silva' / 'Por ...' never match. A running author footer next to page numbers ('- 1 -' on separate blank-line-delimited lines) stays as a direction; only the page numbers are marked. Fix: add re.I to the prefix, e.g. (?i:de|por|texto de|by).

Footer and page-number lines that are NOT separated by blank lines get merged into the previous speech: 'RUI: Mais texto 1.\nTexto de João Silva\n- 1 -' -> RUI text 'Mais texto 1. Texto de João Silva - 1 -'. Page numbers inside speech are then never detected. PDFs often produce exactly this layout.

Stale hardcoded last4 values (d7ba/62c7) and tts_primary=='edge'. The user has since saved app keys (ff29/ba39), so 3 tests fail. These are test-data problems, not app bugs. The test also PUTs bogus keys; this did not change the saved keys (verified).

action_items: mark_non_script: never mark kind=='dialogue' lines through the header path. At minimum, run _header_like on ln.text only, not on the 'NAME — text' string with its built-in em dash. Also require near_break for dialogue; _regular alone is not enough. Re-run tests/test_ensaio_round9.py::test_pedro_sim_regular and ::test_maria_nao_regular.
_header_like author regex: make the 'de|por|texto de|by' prefix case-insensitive so 'Texto de João Silva' footers next to page numbers are marked (test_footer_near_page_numbers).
Optional: in the parser, split standalone page-number or footer lines out of speech continuation (e.g. a line matching RE_PAGE should never be merged into the previous dialogue).
Update tests/test_ensaio_round7.py::TestSettings to stop hardcoding last4 and to stop PUTting bogus keys (use /validate instead).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L325: full = f"{ln.character} — {ln.text}" is then passed to _header_like, which matches '—' through RE_HEADER_WORD, so every repeated dialogue line counts as header-like. This is the RCA for the open bug.
_regular() treats 3 occurrences with equal gaps as positional evidence. Regular spacing is normal in short dialogue scenes, so it should only count for direction-type lines that are also header-like.
server.py is 1555 lines and should be split into modules.

rca of the issue: Repro: POST /api/scripts with text 'ANA: Vens comigo à feira número 0?\nPEDRO: Sim.\nRUI: Eu também vou, na vez 0.' repeated 3 times (i=0..2). Result: lines 1, 4 and 7 become kind=foreign with text 'PEDRO — Sim.' and character=None. Cause: the dialogue group string contains '—', so _header_like is True; the occurrences are at positions 1, 4, 7 (gaps 3, 3), so _regular is True; headers.update marks them. The e1 test passes only because its PEDRO lines are irregularly spaced. Mitigation: exclude dialogue from header detection, or evaluate _header_like on the raw text and require near_break.
